main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snow-covered roof slope above a log front wall with a door, two shuttered windows, icicles and a stone chimney
top_band: Snow roof, white to pale blue-grey with a lighter eave rim, rows ~8-34 in the middle column; the chimney is a small detail on top
evidence: Reading the middle column: the snow roof slope (rows 8-34) is a large, clearly visible roof surface, like the reference houses' roofs. It ends in a bright snow eave lip with icicles at rows 33-36. A dark eave shadow follows at rows 37-39. Below that is the log wall face (rows 40-62) with an inset plank door, windows with blue shutters and snow sills, and horizontal log ends. Top and front are both clearly drawn, with no receding side faces.

style.evidence: The snow has about 5 steps (white, pale blue, light grey-blue, mid blue-grey, shadow) with clumpy, mottled texture and per-lump variation. The wood is shaded in several browns with grain and log-end detail. The door has iron bands and a handle, and the windows have warm gradient glows with blue shutters. Outlines are dark brown beside wood, with no uniform black outline. Tile density matches the reference houses. There are no large flat fills.
